title: Test score cutoff and college enrollment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Sharp Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD)**

This is a classic sharp RDD setup where treatment (automatic college admission eligibility) is deterministically assigned by whether a student's test score crosses a known cutoff (0.5). The key idea is that students just above and just below the cutoff are essentially identical in all observable and unobservable characteristics, so any discontinuous jump in enrollment at the cutoff can be attributed to the treatment.

**Key Assumptions:**
1. **No manipulation of the running variable:** Students cannot precisely manipulate their test scores to sort around the cutoff (testable via McCrary density test).
2. **Continuity of potential outcomes:** In the absence of treatment, the conditional expectation of enrollment would be continuous through the cutoff.
3. **Sharp assignment:** Treatment is a deterministic function of the running variable — all students at or above 0.5 are treated, all below are not.

I will estimate local linear regressions within various bandwidths, use the `rdrobust` package for optimal bandwidth selection and bias-corrected inference, and conduct robustness checks including placebo cutoffs, bandwidth sensitivity, and a density test.

## 2. R Code

```r
# =============================================================
# Sharp RDD: Test Score Cutoff and College Enrollment
# =============================================================

# Install packages if needed
for (pkg in c("rdrobust", "rddensity", "ggplot2")) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(pkg)
}

library(rdrobust)
library(rddensity)
library(ggplot2)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and inspect data
# --------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s26_data.csv")
cat("=== Data Summary ===\n")
str(df)
summary(df)
cat("\nN =", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("N treated =", sum(df$treated), "\n")
cat("N control =", sum(1 - df$treated), "\n")
cat("Mean Y (treated):", mean(df$y[df$treated == 1]), "\n")
cat("Mean Y (control):", mean(df$y[df$treated == 0]), "\n")

# Center the running variable at the cutoff
cutoff <- 0.5
df$X <- df$running_var - cutoff

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Visualization: RD Plot
# --------------------------------------------------
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = running_var, y = y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = cutoff, linetype = "dashed", color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_smooth(data = subset(df, running_var < cutoff), method = "loess", 
              color = "blue", se = TRUE) +
  geom_smooth(data = subset(df, running_var >= cutoff), method = "loess", 
              color = "blue", se = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "RD Plot: Enrollment vs. Test Score",
       x = "Standardized Test Score", y = "Enrollment (y)") +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave("experiments/exp_b/data/rd_plot.png", p, width = 8, height = 5)
cat("\nRD plot saved.\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Main RDD Estimation using rdrobust
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n=== MAIN RESULT: rdrobust with optimal bandwidth ===\n")
rd_main <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = cutoff)
summary(rd_main)

cat("\n--- Key Results ---\n")
cat("RD Estimate (conventional):", rd_main$coef[1], "\n")
cat("RD Estimate (bias-corrected):", rd_main$coef[2], "\n")
cat("Robust 95% CI: [", rd_main$ci[3, 1], ",", rd_main$ci[3, 2], "]\n")
cat("Optimal bandwidth (h):", rd_main$bws[1, 1], "\n")
cat("N (left of cutoff in bw):", rd_main$N_h[1], "\n")
cat("N (right of cutoff in bw):", rd_main$N_h[2], "\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Manual Local Linear Regression (within bandwidth)
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n=== Manual Local Linear Regressions ===\n")

bandwidths <- c(0.1, 0.15, 0.2, 0.25, 0.3)
results <- data.frame(bandwidth = numeric(), estimate = numeric(), 
                       se = numeric(), pval = numeric(), n = numeric())

for (bw in bandwidths) {
  sub <- df[abs(df$X) <= bw, ]
  if (nrow(sub) < 20) next
  mod <- lm(y ~ treated * X, data = sub)
  coef_est <- coef(mod)["treated"]
  se_est <- summary(mod)$coefficients["treated", "Std. Error"]
  pv <- summary(mod)$coefficients["treated", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
    bandwidth = bw, estimate = coef_est, se = se_est, pval = pv, n = nrow(sub)
  ))
}

cat("\nLocal Linear Regression Results Across Bandwidths:\n")
print(results, row.names = FALSE)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. Using the near_cutoff variable (bw = 0.3)
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n=== Estimation using near_cutoff sample (±0.3) ===\n")
sub_near <- df[df$near_cutoff == 1, ]
mod_near <- lm(y ~ treated * X, data = sub_near)
cat("N in near_cutoff sample:", nrow(sub_near), "\n")
summary(mod_near)
cat("RD estimate (near_cutoff):", coef(mod_near)["treated"], "\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. Polynomial specifications (robustness)
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n=== Polynomial Robustness (full sample) ===\n")
for (p_order in 1:3) {
  if (p_order == 1) {
    mod_p <- lm(y ~ treated * X, data = df)
  } else if (p_order == 2) {
    mod_p <- lm(y ~ treated * (X + I(X^2)), data = df)
  } else {
    mod_p <- lm(y ~ treated * (X + I(X^2) + I(X^3)), data = df)
  }
  est <- coef(mod_p)["treated"]
  se <- summary(mod_p)$coefficients["treated", "Std. Error"]
  pv <- summary(mod_p)$coefficients["treated", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  cat(sprintf("Order %d: Estimate = %.4f, SE = %.4f, p = %.4f\n", p_order, est, se, pv))
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 7. Triangular kernel weights (manual)
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n=== Triangular Kernel Weighted Local Linear (bw = 0.2) ===\n")
bw_tri <- 0.2
sub_tri <- df[abs(df$X) <= bw_tri, ]
sub_tri$weight <- 1 - abs(sub_tri$X) / bw_tri
mod_tri <- lm(y ~ treated * X, data = sub_tri, weights = weight)
cat("RD estimate (triangular kernel, bw=0.2):", coef(mod_tri)["treated"], "\n")
cat("SE:", summary(mod_tri)$coefficients["treated", "Std. Error"], "\n")
cat("p-value:", summary(mod_tri)$coefficients["treated", "Pr(>|t|)"], "\n")

# --------------------------------------------------
# 8. McCrary Density Test (manipulation check)
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n=== McCrary Density Test (rddensity) ===\n")
density_test <- rddensity(X = df$running_var, c = cutoff)
summary(density_test)
cat("Density test p-value:", density_test$test$p_jk, "\n")
if (density_test$test$p_jk > 0.05) {
  cat("=> No evidence of manipulation at the cutoff (good).\n")
} else {
  cat("=> WARNING: Possible manipulation at the cutoff.\n")
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 9. Placebo Cutoff Tests
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n=== Placebo Cutoff Tests ===\n")
placebo_cutoffs <- c(0.3, 0.4, 0.6, 0.7)
for (pc in placebo_cutoffs) {
  tryCatch({
    rd_placebo <- rdrobust(y = df$y, x = df$running_var, c = pc)
    cat(sprintf("Placebo cutoff = %.1f: Estimate = %.4f, Robust p = %.4f\n",
                pc, rd_placebo$coef[1], rd_placebo$pv[3]))
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("Placebo cutoff = %.1f: Could not estimate (%s)\n", pc, e$message))
  })
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 10. Summary of findings
# --------------------------------------------------
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("  SUMMARY OF SHARP RDD ANALYSIS\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat(sprintf("Main RD estimate (rdrobust, bias-corrected): %.4f\n", rd_main$coef[2]))
cat(sprintf("Robust 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n", rd_main$ci[3, 1], rd_main$ci[3, 2]))
cat(sprintf("Robust p-value: %.4f\n", rd_main$pv[3]))
cat(sprintf("Optimal bandwidth: %.4f\n", rd_main$bws[1, 1]))
cat(sprintf("Density test p-value: %.4f\n", density_test$test$p_jk))
cat("========================================\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Sign:** I expect a **positive** RD estimate. Crossing the automatic admission threshold should increase college enrollment, since eligible students face lower barriers (guaranteed admission removes uncertainty).

**Magnitude:** Given that `y` appears to be a continuous proxy for enrollment (not strictly binary — note the negative values in the preview), the treatment effect likely represents a meaningful jump. Based on the data preview:
- Treated observations have y ≈ 0.3–0.5
- Control observations have y ≈ -0.1 to 0.2

I expect the **LATE at the cutoff to be approximately 0.15–0.35** units. This represents the causal effect of crossing the automatic admission threshold on enrollment for students right at the margin.

**Robustness expectations:**
- The estimate should be relatively stable across different bandwidths (0.1–0.3), though precision will decrease with narrower bandwidths.
- The McCrary density test should show no evidence of manipulation (p > 0.05), since students typically cannot precisely control standardized test scores.
- Placebo cutoffs at 0.3, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.7 should show **no significant discontinuities**, confirming that the jump is specific to the actual policy cutoff at 0.5.
- Higher-order polynomial specifications should yield similar point estimates, though with wider confidence intervals.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Sharp RDD — test score cutoff; continuity of running variable required; McCrary density test
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Scoring above cutoff significantly increases college enrollment
